subject: Meteorology
title: Islamic Golden Age Contributions
description: A micro-lesson that makes Islamic Golden Age Contributions usable.

hook.text: In the Islamic Golden Age, scholars preserved and expanded Greek meteorological knowledge—adding rigorous observation.

buildup.text: Ibn al-Haytham (Alhazen) studied atmospheric refraction—explaining why the Sun appears flattened near the horizon.

discovery.text: Al-Kindi wrote on tides and atmospheric phenomena—among the first to treat weather as a subject for systematic inquiry.

twist.text: These scholars translated and refined Aristotle—their Arabic texts later re-entered Europe and fueled the Renaissance.

climax.text: Without this preservation and refinement, much of Greek weather knowledge would have been lost to medieval Europe.

punchline.text: They saved the old knowledge—and added their own breakthroughs.

quiz.question: What did Ibn al-Haytham study relating to meteorology?
